exact_quote: Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.
context_before: PDF page 400: section 9.7.13.2 Control Flow Instructions: @; rubric '@'; 'Predicated execution.'; Syntax '@{!}p instruction;'
context_after: PDF page 400: Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction'; Examples 'setp.eq.f32 p,y,0; // is y zero?' / '@!p div.f32 ratio,x,y // avoid division by zero'.
reason_for_inclusion: EXPLICIT normative clause for BLOCK-2: the predication construct @{!}p (section 9.7.13.2) states that threads with a False guard predicate 'do nothing', and its Semantics is 'If {!}p then instruction'. Section 9.7.1.1's add Examples include '@p add.u32 x,y,z;', so this predication rule applies to value-writing add.u32. This is the explicit machine-state-effect statement that the v1 supplement could not find; it determines that when the complete guard expression evaluates false the guarded instruction is not executed and the thread performs no action.
